name: api_complianceDetailsOfDevice
description: **Tool Dependency: CRITICAL**  This tool retrieves DETAILED compliance report information for a SPECIFIC device. Use this tool only when the user asks for compliance DETAILS, a compliance breakdown, a full compliance report, compliance by type, remediation information, severity, sourceInfoList, ackStatus, or message for a device.  Do not use this tool when the user asks for the compliance status/state of a device and does not request details or a breakdown. For "compliance state", "compliance status", or "get device compliance state/status" questions, use `api_getComplianceStatus` instead.  **REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:** You MUST call `get_device_details` BEFORE calling `api_complianceDetailsOfDevice`. This is non-negotiable.  **Step-by-step process:**  1. First, invoke `get_device_details` with the device name or IP address to resolve the device UUID 2. Extract the UUID from the `get_device_details` response 3. Then, invoke `api_complianceDetailsOfDevice` with the `deviceUuid` parameter set to the resolved UUID  **Exception:** If the user explicitly provides a valid device UUID in their request, you may skip step 1 and use the provided UUID directly in `api_complianceDetailsOfDevice`.  **Use Cases - Pick this tool for questions like:** - "Get compliance details of device 50.40.1.45" - "Show me detailed compliance information for device core-router" - "What are the compliance details of device 192.168.1.100" - "Get full compliance report for the device" - "Show compliance breakdown for device xyz"  **VIOLATION TERMINOLOGY (device-scoped) — route here:** Treat "violation", "violations", "compliance violation(s)", "what is violating compliance", "why is device non-compliant", "what is making device non-compliant", "reasons device is non-compliant", and device-scoped "compliance issues" as requests for device compliance DETAILS — use this tool (after `get_device_details`). This includes type- or template-qualified device violations such as syslog violations, template/config violations (e.g., template ACL-config), network-profile (wireless) violations, and network-settings violations for a SPECIFIC device, plus acknowledged/open violation filters. A device referenced by IP address or hostname is a NETWORK DEVICE — resolve it with `get_device_details`; do NOT ask the user to clarify whether it is a network device or a client. These compliance violations are NOT Assurance health issues — do NOT use `get_issues`/`understand_issues`.  **DEFAULT (general violations / details) — call with deviceUuid ONLY; do NOT over-filter:** For a general request for a device's violations or compliance details that does NOT name a specific compliance type and does NOT ask for an intended-vs-actual / config diff — e.g. "what are the violations for device X", "give me the violations, give me details", "show compliance details / breakdown", "why is the device non-compliant" — call this tool with ONLY the deviceUuid. The category, complianceType, status, remediationSupported and diffList parameters are ALL OPTIONAL filters; leave them UNSET by default. Setting any of them narrows the result to a single type/status and will HIDE violations of other types — for example scoping to complianceType/category RUNNING_CONFIG hides NETWORK_SETTINGS (and other) violations and makes the device look like it has "no violations". Set complianceType/category ONLY when the user explicitly names a compliance type (e.g. "network settings", "image", "PSIRT", "running config"); set status ONLY when the user explicitly filters by a status; set remediationSupported ONLY when the user explicitly asks about remediation support. NEVER default complianceType or category to RUNNING_CONFIG. "Give me details" / "details" means the normal detailed report — it does NOT by itself mean a config diff, so do NOT set diffList=true for it.  **COMPLIANCE TYPE & CATEGORY MAPPING — use this to pick the CORRECT complianceType/category when the user names a specific concern; do NOT reflexively choose RUNNING_CONFIG:** The word "config" alone does NOT mean RUNNING_CONFIG. RUNNING_CONFIG means ONLY a startup-vs-running configuration mismatch (config drift). Templates, CLI/feature templates, network profiles, fabric, AVC, workflow, syslog/network-settings, image, PSIRT and EOX are all DIFFERENT compliance types. Only set complianceType/category when the user explicitly names such a concern (for a plain "violations/details" request leave them UNSET per the DEFAULT rule).  Category -> complianceType(s): - INTENT: NETWORK_PROFILE, FABRIC, APPLICATION_VISIBILITY (a.k.a. AVC), WORKFLOW (all design/intent compliance) - RUNNING_CONFIG: RUNNING_CONFIG (a.k.a. startup vs running config mismatch / config drift) - IMAGE: IMAGE (a.k.a. standard / golden image compliance; for full image details use the SWIM APIs — compliance stores only limited detail) - PSIRT: PSIRT (a.k.a. critical security advisories; for full advisory details use the PSIRT APIs — compliance stores only limited detail) - EOX: EOX (a.k.a. end-of-life / end-of-support; for full EOX details use the EOX APIs — compliance stores only limited detail) - NETWORK_SETTINGS: NETWORK_SETTINGS  complianceType -> sub-types / apps (IMPORTANT: these sub-type names are NOT accepted by the API — they exist ONLY to help you choose the parent complianceType. Always pass the PARENT complianceType value, e.g. NETWORK_PROFILE, and NEVER a sub-type such as CLI_TEMPLATE): - RUNNING_CONFIG: RUNNING_CONFIG - PSIRT: PSIRT - IMAGE: IMAGE - NETWORK_RULES: NETWORK_RULES - FABRIC: FABRIC_ROLE, SEGMENT, MULTICAST, AUTHENTICATION_PROFILE, ACCESS_CONTROL_LIST, PORT_CHANNEL, VIRTUAL_NETWORK, WIRELESS - APPLICATION_VISIBILITY (AVC): CBAR_CONFIGURATION, CBAR_CONFIGURATION_CONTROLLER, CBAR_CONFIGURATION_PROTOCOL_DISCOVERY - NETWORK_SETTINGS: GENERAL, WIRELESS - NETWORK_PROFILE: WIRELESS, ROUTING, CLI_TEMPLATE, FEATURE_TEMPLATE - WORKFLOW: UMBRELLA, SITE_TO_SITE_VPN - EOX: SOFTWARE, HARDWARE, MODULE  Mapping user wording -> complianceType (always pass the PARENT type): "CLI template" / "config template" / "feature template" / "ACL-config template" / "template <name> violation" -> NETWORK_PROFILE (sub-type CLI_TEMPLATE or FEATURE_TEMPLATE), NOT RUNNING_CONFIG; "syslog" / "network settings" / "general settings" -> NETWORK_SETTINGS; "fabric" / "segment" / "SGT" / "virtual network" / "port channel" / "access control list" -> FABRIC; "AVC" / "application visibility" / "CBAR" -> APPLICATION_VISIBILITY; "Umbrella" / "site-to-site VPN" -> WORKFLOW; "startup vs running" / "config drift" / "running config" -> RUNNING_CONFIG; "golden image" / "image" -> IMAGE; "security advisory" / "PSIRT" -> PSIRT; "end of life" / "end of support" / "EOX" -> EOX. If the user names a sub-type/app, filter by its PARENT complianceType and then identify the specific sub-type from the returned violations.  **CONFIG DIFF — set diffList=true ONLY for explicit intended-vs-actual questions:** Do NOT set diffList=true (and do NOT add a complianceType) for a plain "violations" or "details" request — see the DEFAULT rule above. The DEFAULT response (diffList omitted or false) lists violations but does NOT contain the per-attribute intended (expected / should-be) versus configured (actual / present) values. To answer ANY question about what SHOULD have been configured versus what IS configured now — e.g. "what should have been configured and what is present now", "intended vs actual configuration", "expected vs current config", "show the config diff / difference", "side-by-side comparison", "what changed", "what is missing", or the exact configuration of a specific violation instance (such as a telemetry subscription id or a feature) — you MUST call this tool with diffList=true together with the relevant complianceType (e.g. RUNNING_CONFIG for startup-vs-running / config drift, or NETWORK_SETTINGS). Only diffList=true returns the diffList array, where each entry has an op (add/remove/update) plus the intended value and the configured value. NEVER answer such questions from the default (non-diff) response, NEVER invent intended/current values, and NEVER claim the API cannot provide the diff or that the user must use the compliance dashboard — set diffList=true and read the diffList.  **CLI TEMPLATE (config template) VIOLATIONS — actual content is NOT available here:** Even with diffList=true, the response does NOT include the actual CLI template violation content (the specific configuration lines/commands), because that content can be extremely large. For CLI template compliance you may report THAT the device is non-compliant for the template/config type and name the affected complianceType, but you CANNOT list, enumerate, or reconstruct the exact violating CLI lines from this tool, and you must NEVER fabricate them. When the user specifically asks for an in-depth analysis or the actual line-by-line details of CLI template violations, tell them to try Deep Reasoning mode, which provides detailed CLI template violation analysis. Do not surface this suggestion for ordinary compliance questions — only when the user asks for the actual CLI template violation content or an in-depth template analysis.

name: api_countsGlobalIPAddressPools
description: Returns the total count of global IP address pools.  PRECEDENCE Apply sections in order. Higher sections override lower sections when they conflict.  S0 Scope and hard boundaries S0.1 Count-only tool for global pools. S0.2 This tool is not site-scoped; ignore site filters. S0.3 Do not use this tool as a detail/list source.  S1 Invocation rules S1.1 Pure count intent (for example, 'how many global pools'): call this tool directly. S1.2 Filter/detail/list intent: use retrieval APIs instead of this count tool as the primary source. S1.3 If user says 'pools' without specifying global vs subpool (or asks about both), call both api_countsGlobalIPAddressPools and api_countsIPAddressSubpools.  S2 Pairing rule with retrieval S2.1 When rendering global-pool lists from api_retrievesGlobalIPAddressPools, call this tool to provide total-result context. S2.2 Use count-line formatting consistent with retrieval rules (for example, 'Showing 10 out of {total} results.' or offset form).  S3 Output format S3.1 For count answers, return Markdown text. S3.2 Never use build_key_value_set. S3.3 Markdown-context requirement: never return widget-only output. If output includes KeyValueSet, response shape must include Markdown context as [Markdown intro, KeyValueSet, Markdown summary].  S4 Prohibitions S4.1 Do not call retrieval APIs when user asks only for a simple total count. S4.2 Do not present count output as pool details.

name: api_countsIPAddressSubpools
description: Returns the total count of IP address subpools.  PRECEDENCE Apply sections in order. Higher sections override lower sections when they conflict.  S0 Scope and hard boundaries S0.1 Count-only tool for subpools. S0.2 Do not use this tool as a detail/list source. S0.3 If site is specified, count only subpools whose siteId exactly matches that site (no parent/child expansion unless explicitly requested).  S1 Invocation rules S1.1 Pure count intent (for example, 'how many subpools'): call this tool directly. S1.2 Filter/detail/list intent: use retrieval APIs instead of this count tool as the primary source. S1.3 If user says 'pools' without specifying global vs subpool (or asks about both), call both api_countsGlobalIPAddressPools and api_countsIPAddressSubpools.  S2 Pairing rule with retrieval S2.1 When rendering subpool lists from api_retrievesIPAddressSubpools, call this tool to provide total-result context. S2.2 Use count-line formatting consistent with retrieval rules (for example, 'Showing 10 out of {total} results.' or offset form).  S3 Output format S3.1 For count answers, return Markdown text. S3.2 Never use build_key_value_set. S3.3 Markdown-context requirement: never return widget-only output. If output includes KeyValueSet, response shape must include Markdown context as [Markdown intro, KeyValueSet, Markdown summary].  S4 Prohibitions S4.1 Do not call retrieval APIs when user asks only for a simple total count. S4.2 Do not present count output as subpool details.

name: api_countsSubpoolsOfAGlobalIPAddressPool
description: Counts the number of IP address subpools within a specific global IP address pool.  PRECEDENCE Apply sections in order. Higher sections override lower sections when they conflict.  S0 Scope and hard boundaries S0.1 Count-only tool for subpools under one specific global pool. S0.2 Use only when user explicitly asks for number/count of subpools in a given global pool (by name or UUID). S0.3 Do not use this tool as a detail/list source.  S1 Invocation rules S1.1 Required parameter: globalIpAddressPoolId must be a valid UUID. S1.2 If UUID is provided, call this tool directly. S1.3 If global pool name is provided, resolve UUID via api_retrievesGlobalIPAddressPools, then call this tool with resolved UUID. S1.4 If user explicitly says 'global pool' and asks for subpool count, prefer this tool path (do not retrieve subpools list). S1.5 If user does not specify global vs subpool, do not use this tool as primary; follow dual retrieval/disambiguation path.  S2 Resolution and pairing behavior S2.1 Name-to-UUID resolution is mandatory when identifier is not UUID. S2.2 Do not ask user for UUID if name lookup can resolve it. S2.3 Do not call this tool with non-UUID name strings in globalIpAddressPoolId.  S3 Output format S3.1 For count answers, return Markdown text. S3.2 Never use build_key_value_set. S3.3 Markdown-context requirement: never return widget-only output. If output includes KeyValueSet, response shape must include Markdown context as [Markdown intro, KeyValueSet, Markdown summary].  S4 Prohibitions and non-goals S4.1 Use this tool for count results only; use retrieval APIs when user asks for subpool list/details. S4.2 This API is not required to determine whether a global pool is unused. S4.3 Unused/empty global pool definition: global pool is unused iff assignedAddresses == 0.

name: api_getComplianceDetail
description: LIST, SHOW, or IDENTIFY which specific devices are compliant or non-compliant. Returns detailed device compliance records including compliance type, status, state, last sync/update time, and remediation support.  NOT for counting. For count/total/how-many questions, use `api_getComplianceStatusCount` (global counts) or `api_getComplianceDetailCount` (type-specific counts).  Use this API ONLY when the user asks to LIST, SHOW, or IDENTIFY WHICH SPECIFIC devices are compliant or non-compliant — i.e., the user wants to see device names, IPs, or details, NOT a count. Examples: "Which devices are compliant?", "List compliant devices", "Show non-compliant devices", "Show me the non-compliant devices for IMAGE", "List devices failing critical security advisory compliance".  **NATURAL LANGUAGE → complianceType ENUM MAPPING:** "critical security advisory" / "security advisory compliance" / "PSIRT" → complianceType=PSIRT (NOTE: this refers to PSIRT *compliance type* for device compliance checks, NOT the separate `api_getSecurityAdvisories*` tools which retrieve advisory details, CVEs, and fix versions). "running config" / "RUNNING_CONFIG" → RUNNING_CONFIG. "image" / "IMAGE" → IMAGE. "end of life" / "EOX" → EOX. "network profile" / "NETWORK_PROFILE" → NETWORK_PROFILE. "network settings" / "NETWORK_SETTINGS" → NETWORK_SETTINGS. "fabric" / "segment" / "SGT" / "virtual network" / "access control list" → FABRIC. "application visibility" / "AVC" / "CBAR" → APPLICATION_VISIBILITY. "Umbrella" / "site-to-site VPN" → WORKFLOW. IMPORTANT: the word "config" alone does NOT mean RUNNING_CONFIG — RUNNING_CONFIG is ONLY a startup-vs-running config mismatch. A CLI/config/feature TEMPLATE (e.g. "ACL-config template", "CLI template violation") maps to NETWORK_PROFILE, NOT RUNNING_CONFIG. Sub-type/app names (CLI_TEMPLATE, FEATURE_TEMPLATE, GENERAL, WIRELESS, CBAR_CONFIGURATION, FABRIC_ROLE, SEGMENT, ACCESS_CONTROL_LIST, UMBRELLA, SITE_TO_SITE_VPN, SOFTWARE, HARDWARE, MODULE, etc.) are NOT accepted by the API; pass only the PARENT complianceType (RUNNING_CONFIG, PSIRT, IMAGE, EOX, FABRIC, APPLICATION_VISIBILITY, NETWORK_SETTINGS, NETWORK_PROFILE, WORKFLOW, NETWORK_RULES). When the user provides underscore-formatted enum values (e.g., NON_COMPLIANT, RUNNING_CONFIG, NETWORK_PROFILE), map them directly to the corresponding `complianceStatus` or `complianceType` parameter.  Do not use `api_getComplianceStatus` for `which/list/show devices are non-compliant` questions; that tool is for high-level device status records. Do not use `api_getComplianceDetailCount` for list/show/which-device questions; a count alone cannot identify devices.  Do not pass unsupported filters such as `siteId`, `siteHierarchy`, tag name, or tag id to this API; it accepts compliance filters and `deviceUuid` only and cannot enforce site or tag scope by itself.  For site-scoped compliance questions, first call `api_getSites` when needed, then call `get_device_details` with the resolved site hierarchy/name, extract device UUIDs, and call `api_getComplianceDetail` with `deviceUuid` as a comma-separated UUID list and `complianceStatus`.  For every tag-qualified compliance question, call `api_getTag(name=<tag name>)` and then `api_getTagMembersById(id=<tag UUID>, memberType="networkdevice" or "device")` before this compliance call; calling this API before `api_getTagMembersById` is invalid for tag-qualified compliance queries, even if `get_device_details` exposes `tagNames`.  Critical rule for combined site + tag questions: the tag-member lookup is required for grounding the tag, but do not pass all tag-member UUIDs directly to this API. Build the requested-site UUID set from `get_device_details(siteHierarchy=<site>, views=["configuration"])`, then keep only those site records whose `tagNames` contains the requested tag; if `tagNames` is unavailable, intersect the tag-member UUID set with the site UUID set. Pass exactly and only that final intersection in `deviceUuid`. Never include same-tag devices from other sites, and never call this API with a superset and filter after the compliance call. If the final intersection has one device, `deviceUuid` must contain that one UUID only, with no comma. For user-facing answers and `build_table` calls, count or list only devices whose UUID is in the final filtered set used for the compliance call.  For device-listing questions, including when the filtered site/tag intersection has exactly one device, the compliance-detail call should use the default limit.  For site-scoped count questions such as "How many devices are compliant in BGL 17" or "count compliant devices at <site>", first resolve the site devices via `get_device_details`, then call `api_getComplianceDetail` with the scoped `deviceUuid` list and the requested `complianceStatus`, and compute the count from the returned detail records. This site-scoped pattern is acceptable because the device set is pre-filtered and bounded. This site-scoped counting workaround applies ONLY to STATUS counts (compliant/non-compliant) with NO compliance TYPE specified. If a compliance TYPE (e.g., RUNNING_CONFIG, IMAGE, PSIRT, NETWORK_SETTINGS, NETWORK_PROFILE, EOX) is specified together with a site/building/floor/area/tag for a count/how-many/number-of question (e.g., 'how many devices have running config mismatch under BGL 16'), do NOT count via get_device_details + api_getComplianceDetail; instead respond that a per-site count for that compliance type cannot be computed due to API limitations. For global (unscoped) count questions, always use `api_getComplianceStatusCount` or `api_getComplianceDetailCount` instead.  **VIOLATION TERMINOLOGY (site-scoped) — route here:** Treat site-scoped "violations", "compliance violations", "network-settings violations", "non-compliant findings", and "open/acknowledged violations under <site>" as compliance-detail requests — first call `api_getSites` (when needed) and `get_device_details(siteHierarchy=<site>)` to resolve device UUIDs, then call this API with `deviceUuid` and `complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT` (add `complianceType` when a type such as NETWORK_SETTINGS/RUNNING_CONFIG/IMAGE/PSIRT is named). These compliance violations are NOT Assurance health issues — do NOT use `get_issues`/`understand_issues` for compliance violation questions.  **DO NOT COUNT BY TYPE FOR A SITE VIA THIS WORKAROUND:** The site-scoped detail-count pattern described above is valid ONLY for STATUS counts (compliant/non-compliant) at a site. Do NOT use a get_device_details + api_getComplianceDetail workaround to COUNT devices by a specific compliance TYPE (e.g., RUNNING_CONFIG, IMAGE, PSIRT, NETWORK_SETTINGS, NETWORK_PROFILE, EOX) scoped to a site/building/floor/area/tag. Site-scoped compliance-TYPE counts are not supported; for such count questions (e.g., "how many devices have running config mismatch under BGL 16") respond that the count cannot be computed for that scope due to API limitations rather than counting from detail records. This restriction applies to COUNT/how-many questions only - LIST/show questions for a compliance type under a site remain valid.

"Count EOX non-compliant" — USE THIS API for all compliance-TYPE-specific count questions.  This API returns the TRUE TOTAL count of devices for a specific compliance TYPE and status. It is the ONLY correct API for compliance-type-specific count questions because it has no pagination limit. `api_getComplianceDetail` MUST NOT be used for counting — it caps at 500 records and produces WRONG results at scale.  **NATURAL LANGUAGE → ENUM MAPPING (critical for correct routing):** "critical security advisory" / "security advisory compliance" / "PSIRT" → complianceType=PSIRT (NOTE: this is about PSIRT *compliance type*, NOT the separate `api_getSecurityAdvisories*` or `api_getCountOfSecurityAdvisories*` tools which deal with advisory details, CVEs, and remediation versions) "running config" / "startup vs running" / "RUNNING_CONFIG" → complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG "image" / "software image" / "IMAGE" → complianceType=IMAGE "end of life" / "end of support" / "EOX" → complianceType=EOX "network profile" / "NETWORK_PROFILE" → complianceType=NETWORK_PROFILE "network settings" / "NETWORK_SETTINGS" → complianceType=NETWORK_SETTINGS "fabric" / "FABRIC" → complianceType=FABRIC "application visibility" / "APPLICATION_VISIBILITY" → complianceType=APPLICATION_VISIBILITY  **MANDATORY — USE THIS API FOR:** - "Count NON_COMPLIANT devices for RUNNING_CONFIG" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG - "How many devices are non-compliant for RUNNING_CONFIG?" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG - "How many devices are non-compliant for running config?" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG - "How many non-compliant devices for IMAGE?" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=IMAGE - "Count NON_COMPLIANT for EOX" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=EOX - "Give me the RUNNING_CONFIG non-compliant count" → complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT, complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG - Any question asking for the count, total, or number of devices by a specific compliance TYPE (RUNNING_CONFIG, IMAGE, PSIRT, EOX, NETWORK_PROFILE, NETWORK_SETTINGS, FABRIC, APPLICATION_VISIBILITY, WORKFLOW) - Any question with underscore-formatted enum values like NON_COMPLIANT, RUNNING_CONFIG, NETWORK_PROFILE, NETWORK_SETTINGS, etc. that asks for a count  **STOP — Do NOT use this API if the question does NOT mention a specific compliance TYPE.** Questions like "How many devices are compliant?", "How many devices are non-compliant?", "Count compliant devices", or "Total non-compliant devices" that do NOT mention RUNNING_CONFIG, IMAGE, PSIRT, EOX, NETWORK_PROFILE, NETWORK_SETTINGS, FABRIC, or APPLICATION_VISIBILITY MUST use `api_getComplianceStatusCount` instead. This API requires a complianceType — without one, use `api_getComplianceStatusCount`.  Do not use this API when the user asks to list, show, or identify which devices match a compliance status or compliance type. For list/show/which-device questions such as "List devices non-compliant for IMAGE" or "Show devices failing IMAGE compliance", use `api_getComplianceDetail` with `complianceStatus`, `complianceType`, and `limit=500` so the response is grounded in device-level detail records.  **NATURAL LANGUAGE (config drift) -> complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG:** "startup vs running config mismatch", "startup versus running config", "running config mismatch", "running config drift", "config drift", and "config mismatch" all map to complianceType=RUNNING_CONFIG for count questions. Route these count questions HERE (with complianceStatus=NON_COMPLIANT) - NOT to any device-configuration, Layer2/Layer3 feature-configuration, or intended-configuration API.  **FILTER LIMITATION - SITE/TAG SCOPING NOT SUPPORTED:** This API returns a GLOBAL total for a complianceType/complianceStatus. It has NO site, siteHierarchy, building, floor, area, or tag parameter and cannot restrict the count to a location or tag. If the user asks for a count of a compliance TYPE scoped to a specific site/building/floor/area/tag (e.g., "how many devices have running config mismatch under BGL 16"), do NOT return the global count as if it were the site count, and do NOT build a get_device_details + api_getComplianceDetail workaround to compute a type count for the site. Instead respond that the count cannot be computed for that scope due to API limitations (for example: "I can't calculate a per-site count for RUNNING_CONFIG compliance because the compliance count API doesn't support site-level filtering."). You may offer the global count or offer to list the non-compliant devices under that site instead.

name: api_getComplianceStatus
description: This tool retrieves high-level device-level compliance status records for all devices or specific device(s). Use this tool when the user asks for the compliance status/state of a device, or asks to list actual device compliance status records.  Do not answer requests such as "list all device compliance statuses" from static knowledge unless the user explicitly asks for possible status values or a glossary of status meanings. For actual device compliance status records, call this API.  Do not use this tool for questions that ask to list, show, or identify which devices are compliant/non-compliant, especially site-scoped, tag-scoped, or compliance-type-specific lists. Use `api_getComplianceDetail` with `limit=500` for those device-listing questions.  **MANDATORY PREREQUISITE:** You MUST call `get_device_details` before `api_getComplianceStatus` when the user provides device name(s) or IP address(es).  **Steps:** 1. If the user provides device name(s) or IP address(es), call `get_device_details` and extract the device UUID(s). 2. If the user provides valid device UUID(s) directly, skip step 1. 3. Call `api_getComplianceStatus` with `deviceUuid` set to the device UUID(s). Use a comma-separated list for multiple devices. 4. If the user does not provide any device identifier and asks for actual device status records, call `api_getComplianceStatus` without `deviceUuid`. 5. For user-facing output, do not show raw `deviceUuid`. Call `get_device_details` with `device_id` set to each returned UUID and include the `managementIpAddress` in the response. The management IP address is mandatory in user-facing output.  **Returns:** Compliance status records for all devices or specified devices. User-facing output MUST include `managementIpAddress`, `complianceStatus`, and `lastUpdateTime`, and MUST NOT show raw `deviceUuid` unless the user explicitly asks for internal device identifiers.  Exact-query examples that MUST use this API, not documentation search: "List all device compliance statuses", "Show all device compliance statuses", "List device compliance status records", and "Get all device compliance states". These ask for live device records, not definitions of possible status values.  Do not use this tool for count/total/"how many" questions. For global count questions like "How many devices are compliant?" or "How many devices are non-compliant?", use `api_getComplianceStatusCount`. For compliance-type-specific counts like "How many non-compliant for RUNNING_CONFIG?", use `api_getComplianceDetailCount`. For site-scoped counts like "How many compliant in BGL 17?", resolve site devices with `get_device_details`, then use `api_getComplianceDetail` with the scoped `deviceUuid` list.

name: api_getConfigurationArchiveDetails
description: **Use Cases - Pick this tool for ANY of these question types about a device's configuration archive / archive history / configuration changes / config drift:** - "When was the last archive of device X?" / "latest archive timestamp" / "most recent archive" - "How many archives / config archives / configuration backups for device X?" - "How many config drifts / configuration drifts / drift entries / drift instances on device X?" - "Was device X changed outside Catalyst Center / outside CatC?" / "out-of-band (OOB) config changes" / "external configuration changes" - "Who made the last config change on device X?" / "which user last modified the configuration" - "When was the last startup config / startup-config change on device X?" - "How many devices in site Y had config changes in the last N days/hours?"  Returns the historical device configurations (running, startup, vlan) by specified criteria. The response is an array with one entry per device. Within each device entry the `versions` array is ordered chronologically OLDEST FIRST: `versions[0]` is the EARLIEST archive for that device and `versions[-1]` (the LAST element of the array) is the MOST RECENT / LATEST archive.  **CRITICAL - How to find the LATEST archive. This applies IDENTICALLY to every phrasing that asks for the newest/last/most-recent archive, including 'when was my last archive done', 'when was the last archive', 'last archive', 'most recent archive', 'latest archive timestamp', 'last change', 'who made last config change', 'last startup-config change'. Treat ALL of these phrasings exactly the same.**  STEP 0 (MANDATORY): The `versions` array is sorted OLDEST-FIRST and the API returns only the FIRST `limit` versions. If you pass a small `limit` (e.g. 10) you will receive only the 10 OLDEST archives and the true latest will be missing. Therefore for ANY latest/last/most-recent/count/history question you MUST pass `limit` = 50 (the maximum supported) so the newest archives are included. NEVER pass limit=10 for these questions. STEP 1: Look at every element of the `versions` array and read each element's `createdTime` (epoch ms). STEP 2: The LATEST archive is the element with the NUMERICALLY GREATEST `createdTime`. Because the array is sorted oldest-first, this is ALWAYS the LAST element, `versions[-1]`. STEP 3: Answer using ONLY that element. Convert and report ONLY `versions[-1].createdTime`.  HARD RULE - NEVER answer with `versions[0]`. `versions[0]` is the OLDEST archive (often `createdBy == SCHEDULED_FIRST_TIME`) and is the WRONG answer for any 'latest/last/most-recent' question. If you are about to convert or report the smallest/earliest `createdTime`, STOP — you must use the largest/last one instead. When calling a timestamp-conversion helper for a 'latest/last' question, pass ONLY the single `createdTime` value taken from the LAST element `versions[-1]`. Do not pass `versions[0].createdTime`. The total archive count for a device equals the length of its `versions` array.  **CONFIG DRIFT COUNT - how to answer 'how many config drifts / configuration drifts / drift entries / drift instances':** A config drift is simply an ARCHIVED VERSION. The drift count is the TOTAL NUMBER of elements in the `versions` array - i.e. `len(versions)` - counting EVERY version regardless of its `configChangeType` or `createdBy` (include baseline/scheduled snapshots such as `SCHEDULED_FIRST_TIME` and `SCHEDULED`, and every `IN_BAND`/`OUT_OF_BAND` change). Do NOT filter by `configChangeType`. Do NOT use `startupRunningStatus` to determine drift count - `startupRunningStatus` (IN_SYNC / OUT_OF_SYNC) only describes whether the running and startup configs match for a single archived version and is NOT the definition of a config drift; even when every version is `IN_SYNC`, each version still counts as a drift. To answer a drift-count question, report `len(versions)` (remember to fetch with `limit`=50 so all versions are included). COUNT EXACTLY: enumerate the `versions` array element-by-element (assign index 1 to the first element, 2 to the second, and so on) and report the index of the final element. Do NOT estimate or round; the answer must equal the precise number of `versions` entries returned by the API for that device. Each device entry has its OWN `versions` array - count only the `versions` of the requested device; never add the device record itself or entries from other devices to the count.  Out-of-band (OOB) changes are versions where `configChangeType == OUT_OF_BAND`; in-band changes are `IN_BAND`. The user who made a change (when available) is in `versions[*].syslogConfigEventDto[*].userName`. For startup vs running config questions, filter by `fileType` (`RUNNINGCONFIG` or `STARTUPCONFIG`). For time-window questions ('last N days/hours'), pass `createdTime` using the STRICT format `<logicalOp>:<epochMillis>` — operator, then a COLON, then EPOCH MILLISECONDS (13-digit integer). Example: `GT:1781344279000`. NEVER use a dot separator and NEVER pass an ISO/human-readable timestamp (e.g. `GT.2026-06-14T05:46:23.063000` is WRONG). Compute the cutoff instant, convert it to epoch milliseconds, then build `GT:<epochMillis>` (or `LT`/`BT` as appropriate; only GT, LT, BT are supported; `BT` takes two comma-separated epoch-ms values).  **FLEET-WIDE / 'WHICH DEVICES' TIME-WINDOW questions (e.g. 'list the devices that went through any config change in the last 12 hours', 'which devices changed in the last N days', 'how many devices had config changes recently'):** `deviceId` is OPTIONAL. For these fleet-wide questions you can call this tool with ONLY the `createdTime` filter (e.g. `createdTime='GT:<epochMillis>'`) and DO NOT pass `deviceId` unless specifically needed because of a filter. If `deviceId` filter is not provided, the API will return one entry per device that has a matching archive in that window, so a single call answers the whole question. DO NOT first fetch the device inventory / list all devices unless specific filter needs to be applied on the devices. Passing many devices makes the request URL exceed the ~2000-character safe limit and the server returns HTTP 431 'Request Header Fields Too Large' (`deviceId` is sent as a URL query parameter and is capped at 25 comma-separated UUIDs; fleet-wide queries must therefore omit it). Simply omit `deviceId` and let the time filter select the devices.  **PRE-REQUISITE - ONLY for questions scoped to a SPECIFIC named device (an IP, hostname, or serial in the question):** Call `get_device_details` first to resolve that one IP/hostname to a device UUID, then pass it as `deviceId`. Exception: if the user already supplied a valid device UUID, you may skip `get_device_details`. `deviceId` is NOT mandatory - omit it entirely for fleet-wide/time-window questions as described above; never enumerate all devices to populate it.  **Do NOT route 'config drift', 'archive history', 'OOB change', 'who changed', or 'last startup-config change' questions to `api_deviceComplianceStatus`, `api_complianceDetailsOfDevice`, `api_getNetworkDeviceConfigurationFileDetails`, or `api_countOfNetworkDeviceConfigurationFiles` — those tools are for different use cases.**

The following device settings will be enabled when devices are assigned to a site. If Device Controllability is disabled, Catalyst Center does not configure any of the preceding credentials or settings on devices during discovery, at runtime, or during site assignment. However, the telemetry settings and related configuration are pushed when the device is provisioned or when the update Telemetry Settings action is performed. Use this tool only when the user does not specify a particular device, device name, management IP, MAC address, serial number, or networkDeviceId. If the user asks about a bug on a specific device, such as 'details of CSCwd12345 on 50.30.1.9' or 'is device X affected by CSCwd12345', first call get_device_details to resolve the device UUID, then call api_getNetworkBugDeviceForTheBugByNetworkDeviceId with the bug id and resolved networkDeviceId. A CSC ID in a question about bugs is a network bug ID, not a security advisory ID.

Use this tool when the user asks whether a device is affected by a CSC network bug, or asks for details/status of a CSC network bug on a particular device, device name, management IP, MAC address, serial number, or networkDeviceId. Required workflow: if the user provides a device name, IP address, MAC, or serial number instead of a networkDeviceId UUID, first call get_device_details to resolve the device UUID, then call this tool with id set to the CSC bug ID and networkDeviceId set to the resolved device UUID. Do not use api_getNetworkBugById for device-specific bug questions.

name: api_getNetworkBugDevices
description: Get network devices that have network bugs detected by the network bug scan. Use this list tool for requests like 'what devices have bugs?', 'show all devices with network bugs', 'devices with failed bug scans', or 'devices scanned by CX Cloud'. For unqualified devices-with-bugs questions, call this tool with bugCount: 0 and limit: 10 so only devices with at least one detected bug are returned. If you need device names, IPs, models, or site details after this tool returns, call get_device_details only for the returned networkDeviceId values: use device_id for one returned ID, or filters: [{"field":"id","operator":"in","value":[...returned networkDeviceId values...]}] for multiple IDs. Never call get_device_details without a device_id or id filter for this flow, because that widens the result set to devices that do not have network bugs. The final answer must include only devices returned by api_getNetworkBugDevices. Do not use this tool for 'how many devices have bugs?' count questions; use api_getCountOfNetworkBugDevices with bugCount: 0 for counts.

name: api_getNetworkBugDevicesForTheBug
description: Get the network devices affected by a specific network bug ID. Use this tool for questions like 'which devices are affected by CSCwd12345?', 'what devices are impacted by bug CSCwr77118?', or 'show devices with failed scans for CSCwd12345'. A CSC ID in a bug-impact question is a network bug ID, not a security advisory ID. Use scanStatus when the user asks for failed, successful, in-progress, or not-scanned bug scans. Do not use security advisory network-device tools for CSC network bug device-impact questions unless the user explicitly says security advisory, PSIRT, Cisco advisory, or CVE.

name: api_getNetworkBugs

Use this list tool for questions that ask which network bugs exist, which bugs are detected, which severe/moderate/catastrophic bugs affect the network, or which bugs affect devices. For any in-my-network, detected, or severity-specific network bug list question, explicitly pass deviceCount: 0 so the list includes only bugs with at least one affected device. Examples: 'List all network bugs detected' -> deviceCount: 0 and limit: 10; 'Show severe network bugs' -> severity: SEVERE, deviceCount: 0, and limit: 10. Do not omit deviceCount, because omitting it may return all known bug records including bugs with no affected devices.

name: api_getSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice
description: **Tool Dependency: CRITICAL**  This tool retrieves DETAILED information about each security advisory affecting a specific network device, including advisory IDs, CVEs, severity, remediation versions, and more. The response includes a comprehensive list of all advisories impacting the device with full details for each advisory.  **REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:** You MUST call `get_device_details` BEFORE calling `api_getSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice`. This is non-negotiable.  **Step-by-step process:**  1. First, invoke `get_device_details` with the device name or IP address to resolve the device UUID 2. Extract the UUID from the `get_device_details` response 3. Then, invoke `api_getSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice` with the `networkDeviceId` parameter set to the resolved UUID  **Exception:** If the user explicitly provides a valid device UUID in their request, you may skip step 1 and use the provided UUID directly in `api_getSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice`.

name: api_getTag
description: **TAG DEFINITION LISTING RULE:** - Use this API to enumerate existing tag definitions when the user asks for available, existing, default/system, or custom/user-created tags. - For an unfiltered tag-definition inventory, omit both `name` and `systemTag`. - Use `systemTag=true` only for system-created/default tag definitions, and `systemTag=false` only for user-created/custom tag definitions. - Do not use `api_getTagResourceTypes` for tag-definition inventory; that tool returns taggable object categories, not existing tag records. **TAG PHRASE INTERPRETATION RULE:** - When the user says `tag <value>`, `tagged <value>`, `tagged with <value>`, `tagged as <value>`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag <value>`, or `in tag <value>`, treat `<value>` as a tag name and pass that literal value to `name`. - Tag names can look like switch names, device labels, site names, interface labels, operational states, or camelCase words. The presence of words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down inside the value does not change it into a device/site/interface lookup when the user introduced it as a tag. - Do not reinterpret a tag name as a switch, hostname, site, interface, IP address, or inventory search term.  **NAMED-TAG RESOLVER RULE:** - Use this API first when the user gives a human-readable tag name and asks for devices, ports, interfaces, or member counts inside that tag. - This tool resolves the tag name to a tag UUID. It is not the final answer tool for member questions. - After a successful response containing an `id`, immediately call exactly one companion member tool:   - `api_getTagMembersById` for list/show/get/find/which/what member requests.   - `api_getTagMemberCount` for count/how-many/total/number member requests. - For device membership, the companion tool must use `memberType="networkdevice"`. - For port or interface membership, the companion tool must use `memberType="interface"`. - Repeating `api_getTag` with the same tag name after a UUID has been returned is incorrect; move to the companion member tool.  **DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:** - Do not use `api_getTagCount` for named-tag member counts; it counts tag definitions, not members. - Do not use `api_getInterfaces` or generic device/interface inventory tools to answer which resources are in one tag. - Do not use inverse association tools when the user wants tag-to-member lookup. - Do not start with `api_getTagResourceTypes`, site tools, or knowledge-base fallback for live named-tag membership questions. - Do not reuse the tag name as a site name, device name, interface name, IP address, or UUID.  **TAG + SITE OR COMPLIANCE NOTE:** - If a request combines a named tag with a site or compliance filter, this API still only resolves the tag UUID. Ground the tag by calling `api_getTagMembersById` with that UUID before applying site or compliance filtering.

name: api_getTagById
description: Returns tag specified by Id

name: api_getTagCount
description: **TAG PHRASE EXCLUSION:** - If the user asks how many/count/total/number of devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces are `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag <value>`, or `in tag <value>`, do not use this tool. The value is a tag name for a member-count workflow, not a tag-definition count filter. - Use `api_getTag` followed by `api_getTagMemberCount` for named-tag member counts, even when the tag name looks like a switch, device, site, port, interface, or operational state.  "How many tag definitions exist?" "Count user-created tags" "How many system tags are there?" — USE THIS API only for counting TAG DEFINITIONS.  This API returns the count of tag definitions. It does NOT return the number of devices, ports, or interfaces inside a tag.  **MANDATORY — USE THIS API FOR:** - total tag count - count of user-created or system-created tags - how many tag definitions match a given name - questions about whether duplicate tag definitions exist  **DO NOT USE THIS API FOR:** - "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?" - "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?" - "How many ports are tagged with <tag name>?" - "How many interfaces are tagged with <tag name>?" - "How many ports/interfaces are tagged with <tag name>?" - "List devices in tag <tag name>" - "Show interfaces in tag <tag name>" - Any named-tag membership question  **NEGATIVE FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES:** - User: "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?" -> do NOT use `api_getTagCount`; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount` - User: "How many ports are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use `api_getTagCount`; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount`  For named-tag member counts, the correct route is: 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. extract the UUID 3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`  **WRONG ROUTING TO AVOID:** - Never use `api_getTagCount` just because the question contains "count", "how many", or "total". - Never use `api_getTagCount` for device-count or interface-count questions inside a tag. - STOP and switch to `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount` when the question is about members of a named tag.

name: api_getTagMemberCount
description: **TAG MEMBER COUNT TOOL:** - Select this tool together with `api_getTag` when the user provides a human-readable tag name and asks how many, count, total, or number of members are inside that tag. - Execute this tool after `api_getTag` returns the tag UUID. This tool requires a UUID in `id`; never pass the tag name as `id`. - Use this for counts of devices, ports, or interfaces inside one named tag. - Use `memberType="networkdevice"` when counting devices. - Use `memberType="interface"` when counting ports or interfaces. **TAG NAME DISAMBIGUATION:** - If the request uses `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks how many/count/total/number of devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces belong to that value, select this tool with `api_getTag`. - The value introduced by the tag phrase remains a tag name even if it contains words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down. Do not route it to site, device, interface, inventory count, or tag-definition count tools. - For device counts inside the tag, use `memberType="networkdevice"`. For port or interface counts inside the tag, use `memberType="interface"`.  **REQUIRED WORKFLOW:** 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. Extract the returned tag UUID. 3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`  **DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:** - Do not use `api_getTagCount`; that counts tag definitions, not members inside one tag. - Do not use generic device counts, onboarding counts, compliance counts, or field-notice counts for named-tag member counts. - Do not use inverse tag-association tools or generic inventory tools to reconstruct a count indirectly. - Do not leave the workflow at `api_getTag`, and do not keep calling `api_getTag` repeatedly after the UUID has already been resolved. - Do not use this tool for list/show/which member questions; use `api_getTagMembersById` after `api_getTag` instead. - Do not fall back to generic KB guidance for live named-tag count questions.

name: api_getTagMembersById
description: **TAG MEMBER LISTING TOOL:** - Select this tool together with `api_getTag` when the user provides a human-readable tag name and asks to list, show, get, find, identify, or ask what/which members are inside that tag. - Execute this tool after `api_getTag` returns the tag UUID. This tool requires a UUID in `id`; never pass the tag name as `id`. - Use this for tag-to-device and tag-to-interface/tag-to-port listing workflows. - Use `memberType="networkdevice"` when the requested members are devices. - Use `memberType="interface"` when the requested members are ports or interfaces. **TAG NAME DISAMBIGUATION:** - If the request uses `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks which/list/show/get devices, network devices, ports, or interfaces belong to that value, select this tool with `api_getTag`. - The value introduced by the tag phrase remains a tag name even if it contains words like switch, device, site, port, interface, up, or down. Do not route it to site, device, interface, or inventory lookup tools. - For devices or network devices inside the tag, use `memberType="networkdevice"`. For ports or interfaces inside the tag, use `memberType="interface"`.  **REQUIRED WORKFLOW:** 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. Extract the returned tag UUID. 3. `api_getTagMembersById(id=<UUID>, memberType=<networkdevice_or_interface>)`  **DO NOT SUBSTITUTE:** - Do not use this tool for count/how-many/total/number questions; use `api_getTagMemberCount` after `api_getTag` instead. - Do not leave the workflow at `api_getTag`; once the UUID is known, this tool performs the member lookup. - Do not keep calling `api_getTag` repeatedly after the UUID has already been resolved. - Do not use `api_getInterfaces`, generic device inventory, site lookup, resource-type discovery, or inverse tag-association tools when the user wants members of one named tag. - Do not fall back to generic KB guidance for live named-tag membership.  **TAG + SITE OR COMPLIANCE NOTE:** - This API returns tag-scoped members. If the user also names a site or asks for compliance, intersect these tag members with the requested site or compliance filter before forming the final answer.

name: api_getTagResourceTypes
description: **TAG PHRASE EXCLUSION:** - If the user names one tag with `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks for devices, ports, interfaces, or counts, do not use this tool. The request is about members of one tag, not taggable resource categories. - Use `api_getTag` followed by `api_getTagMembersById` or `api_getTagMemberCount` for named-tag membership workflows.  Returns the supported resource categories that can be tagged in Cisco Catalyst Center, such as what kinds of entities are taggable. Use this tool only when the user asks about supported taggable resource types or categories.  **NOT FOR TAG INVENTORY:** - Do not use this tool when the user asks to enumerate existing tag definitions or tag records. - Do not use this tool for system/default tags or user-created/custom tags. - Use `api_getTag` for tag-definition inventory; this tool is only for taggable resource-category capability questions.  This tool does NOT resolve a tag name, does NOT return a tag UUID, and does NOT return the members inside one named tag.  **USE THIS TOOL ONLY FOR:** - "What resource types can be tagged?" - "Which kinds of objects support tags?" - category-level capability questions about taggable entities  **DO NOT USE THIS TOOL FOR:** - "Which devices have tag <tag name>?" - "List devices tagged as <tag name>" - "Get devices under tag <tag name>" - "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?" - any request about the members inside one specific named tag  If the request names one tag and asks for devices, interfaces, ports, or counts, the correct route is: 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. then `api_getTagMembersById` or `api_getTagMemberCount`  **STOP CONDITIONS:** - STOP if the user provided a specific tag name and wants members or counts. - STOP if you are about to loop on resource-type discovery instead of resolving the tag with `api_getTag`.

"What tags are assigned to devices?" "Show device-to-tag mappings" "List tags associated with network devices" — USE THIS API only for DEVICE -> TAGS direction. It answers device-to-tag mapping questions, not tag-to-device membership questions.  **USE THIS API FOR:** - showing tags assigned to devices - listing device-to-tag associations - asking what tags a device or set of devices has  **DO NOT USE THIS API FOR:** - "List devices tagged with <tag name>" - "Please list devices tagged <tag name>" - "Give me the list of devices tagged with <tag name>" - "Which devices have tag <tag name>?" - "What devices are tagged with <tag name>?" - "What are the devices with <tag name> tag?" - "Get devices under tag <tag name>" - "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?" - "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?" - Any request that starts from one named tag and asks for its members or member count  **NEGATIVE FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES:** - User: "Give me the list of devices tagged with <tag name>" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById` - User: "What devices are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById` - User: "What are the devices with <tag name> tag?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById` - User: "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount`  For named-tag membership questions, the correct route is: 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. extract UUID 3. `api_getTagMembersById(id=<UUID>, memberType='networkdevice')`  For named-tag member-count questions, the correct route is: 1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)` 2. extract UUID 3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType='networkdevice')`  **WRONG ROUTING TO AVOID:** - STOP if the user names one specific tag and asks for devices in that tag. - STOP if the user asks for the count of devices in one named tag. - Do not substitute this API for `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById`. - Do not combine this API with `execute_python_code` to reconstruct the members of one named tag.

name: api_retrieveTelemetrySettingsForASite
description: Retrieves effective site telemetry settings for a site: application visibility, application telemetry, wired endpoint data collection, wireless telemetry, SNMP traps, syslog servers, and collectors. Use this tool for site-level telemetry questions, including application visibility on wired access devices, collector type/address/port, whether wired endpoint data collection or wireless telemetry is enabled, whether built-in SNMP/syslog is used, and which external SNMP/syslog servers are set. Call with `_inherited=true` unless the user explicitly asks for only settings configured locally on the site. `_inherited` is only a retrieval option for effective values; it is not a visible answer requirement. Treat phrases like "configured at site", "configured for site", "settings at site", or "site settings" as asking for current effective settings, not local-only settings. For normal all-settings questions, show every returned top-level telemetry setting's effective value. Keep the card compact: use one key-value item per returned top-level telemetry setting, and fold nested details into that setting's value. For `applicationVisibility`, the enabled/disabled status is controlled by `enableOnWiredAccessDevices`; `collector.collectorType` only tells which collector is selected and must not be treated as an enabled flag. If `enableOnWiredAccessDevices` is false, application visibility/application telemetry on wired access devices is disabled even when `collectorType` is `Builtin`. Show the collector as a detail in the same application visibility value. Do not create separate all-settings items for collector type, collector address, collector port, built-in server status, external server address, or enabled flags when those details belong under a parent telemetry setting. For example, keep collector details under application visibility, and keep built-in plus external server details under their SNMP or syslog setting. Do not answer with only local settings, do not omit inherited effective settings, do not say that only syslog is configured, and do not say that all other settings are inherited. For any normal settings question, including all-settings, yes/no, collector, SNMP, or syslog questions, the visible answer must not mention inheritance, inherited from, parent site, source site, local, or locally configured unless the user explicitly asks about inheritance/source or local-only/overridden settings. Do not append parent details in parentheses to values. Omit time range summaries and follow-up offers. For yes/no questions, answer yes or no and include only directly related values such as enabled/disabled status or configured values. When a setting value is a list, show the list entries rather than only the count. For focused questions, answer from the matching field in the returned `response` object and report the concrete setting value first. Only when the user explicitly asks which settings are inherited or where values come from, use inheritance metadata. For those inheritance/source questions, use one consistent table with one row per top-level telemetry setting that has `inheritedSiteName`; columns should be Setting and Inherited from. Use each setting object's own `inheritedSiteName` value. Do not combine parent names into a single value such as Global/San Jose, do not copy inheritance between telemetry objects, do not use `inheritedSiteId`, and do not list local settings as inherited. If a top-level setting has no `inheritedSiteName`, treat it as local.

name: api_retrievesSummaryOfNetworkDeviceLicenses
description:
**Retrieves** the summary of consumed network device licenses.

Use this tool to obtain **aggregate statistics** and license usage counts by type (e.g. 'DNA Advantage' counts).

**CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: SUMMARY ONLY**
This tool returns **ONLY counts**, it does **NOT** return device lists or details. It provides high-level dashboard data.

**Do NOT:**
- Use this tool for queries asking to **list**, **show**, **find**, or **get** details of devices.
- Use this tool if the user needs to know *which* devices have a license. Use `api_readNetworkDeviceLicenses` for that purpose.

**Use Case Limitation:**
Unless the user specifically asks for 'Summary' or 'Breakdown', ALWAYS prefer `api_readNetworkDeviceLicenses` for finding devices.

DO NOT USE FOR SYSTEM-LEVEL QUERIES: This API is ONLY for network device license summaries (switches, routers, APs managed BY Catalyst Center). DO NOT use for "my system", "the system", "CatC", or "Catalyst Center platform" queries - use api_systemLicensingStatus for those instead.

**USE THIS API WHEN:**
- Query asks for network device license summary (devices managed by CatC)
- Need counts of unregistered, out-of-compliance, expired, or expiring DEVICE licenses
- Want aggregated counts of Network/DNA/CNS licenses consumed by managed network devices

**DO NOT USE THIS API WHEN:**
- "How many licenses are consumed by my system?" → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "License usage of my system" → api_systemLicensingStatus  
- "How many licenses have I consumed?" (no device specifics) → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "Show license consumption details" (no device type) → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "What licenses does my CatC use?" → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "How many purchased licenses are there for switch devices?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: SWITCH
- "How many used licenses do I have for routers?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: ROUTER
- "How many licenses are used by managed devices for WLCs?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: UNIFIED_AP
- "Show license usage for WLC device type" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: UNIFIED_AP
- For purchased/used/available license totals by product family (switch/router/WLC/wireless/AP/ISE), use api_getLicenseUsage (NOT this API).

Retrieves the summary of consumed network, DNA, and unified licenses BY MANAGED NETWORK DEVICES (not the CatC system itself), along with the counts of unregistered and out-of-compliance network devices, and expired and expiring network device licenses. This is a network device aggregate view, not a system-level or account-level view.

name: api_returnsTheImageSummaryForTheGivenSite
description:
**Tool Dependency: CRITICAL**

Returns aggregate image statistics (counts of product names, golden/non-golden, imported images, advisor recommendations) for a specific site.

**REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:**
You MUST call `api_getSites` BEFORE calling this tool so you can supply a real `siteId`.

**Step-by-step process:**
1. Call `api_getSites` (typically with `name="Global"`, unless the user specified another hierarchy)
2. Extract the desired site's UUID from the response
3. Call `api_returnsTheImageSummaryForTheGivenSite` with that `siteId`

**Exception:**
If the user explicitly provides a valid site UUID, you may reuse it directly.

**Do NOT:**
- Omit the prerequisite `api_getSites` lookup
- Pass `None`/empty strings for `siteId`
- Attempt to infer or guess a UUID

name: api_systemLicensingLastOperationStatus
description: **Tool Dependency: NONE**  Retrieves the task completion status of the last/most recent licensing operation or task executed for Cisco Catalyst Center system. This is a standalone API with no prerequisites.  **Use Cases:** Use when checking, verifying, or getting the status of completed or in-progress smart licensing operations, tasks, or jobs such as: - System registration operations/tasks (whether system registration completed, succeeded, failed) - System authorization operations/tasks (whether authorization renewal completed) - Any smart licensing related task execution status  **What This API Does:** Returns task execution details: - status: PENDING (task in progress), SUCCESS (task completed successfully), FAILURE (task failed) - isError: true (failed), false (succeeded) - failureReason: explanation of why task failed - errorCode: error identifier if applicable - taskId: unique task identifier - lastUpdate: timestamp of last status update  **IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:** This API provides TASK/OPERATION completion status (whether an operation finished), NOT the current authorization/compliance status of the system. For current system authorization/compliance/registration state (AUTHORIZED, OUT_OF_COMPLIANCE, REGISTERED, etc.), use `api_systemLicensingStatus` instead.  **When to Use:** - After initiating a licensing operation to check if it completed - Troubleshooting failed licensing tasks - Monitoring in-progress licensing operations - Getting the most recent task execution results  **Do NOT:** - Use this API to check current system authorization status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`) - Use this API to check current compliance status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`) - Use this API to get registration status (use `api_systemLicensingStatus`) - Confuse task completion status with system operational status

name: api_theTrendAnalyticsDataForAFabricSiteInTheSpecifiedTimeRange
description: Get health time series for a specific Fabric Site by providing the unique Fabric site id in the url path. The data will be grouped based on the specified trend time interval. If startTime and endTime are not provided, the API defaults to the last 24 hours.  By default: - the number of records returned will be 500. - the records will be sorted in time ascending (`asc`) order  ex: id:93a25378-7740-4e20-8d90-0060ad9a1be0  This API provides the latest health data until the given `endTime`. If data is not ready for the provided endTime, the request will fail with error code `400 Bad Request`, and the error message will indicate the recommended endTime to use to retrieve a complete data set. This behavior may occur if the provided endTime=currentTime, since we are not a real time system. When `endTime` is not provided, the API returns the latest data.  For detailed information about the usage of the API, please refer to the Open API specification document - https://github.com/cisco-en-programmability/catalyst-center-api-specs/blob/main/Assurance/CE_Cat_Center_Org-fabricSiteHealthSummaries-1.0.1-resolved.yaml

name: api_virtualAccountDetails
description:
**Licensing Virtual Account Details** (Tool Dependency: CRITICAL). Retrieve Virtual Account details for a specific Licensing Smart Account.

**Execution Policy (MANDATORY):**
- Use this tool directly for licensing virtual-account queries.
- Do NOT ask users whether they mean Licensing or PnP Smart Accounts.
- Treat this tool as Licensing context only.

**REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:**
You MUST call `api_smartAccountDetails` BEFORE calling `api_virtualAccountDetails`.

**Step-by-step process:**
1. Invoke `api_smartAccountDetails` to retrieve smart accounts.
2. Extract the `id` from the matched smart account.
3. Invoke `api_virtualAccountDetails` with `smart_account_id` set to the resolved ID.
4. If searching for a specific virtual account name and not found, repeat for other Smart Account IDs as needed.

**Do NOT:**
- Use this tool to list Smart Accounts (use `api_smartAccountDetails`)
- Call this tool without a valid Smart Account ID
